messages:
alex: Heads-up: nightly perf job showed a ~+18% tail token latency regression on kv-cache heavy runs. I grabbed an nsys trace (attached) but we should automate collection in CI so we don't miss these.
sam: link? can you drop the artifact path and the run args you used?
alex: s3://perf-artifacts/kvtrace/1765432123/nsys.qdrep (private bucket). Command was basically: `nsys profile -o nsys.qdrep --trace=cuda,nvtx python run_kv_workload.py --model=resnet-like --batch 4 --seq 1024`
mia: thanks. For CI we should capture both cold and warmed traces: cold=first-batch (cache miss), warm=after ~5 iterations (kv cache hot). Otherwise kernel selection looks different.
jordan: +1. Also add environment logging for kernel selection: set `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_LOG_KERNELS=1` so the runtime emits which kernels/quantized paths it chose per layer.
perf-ci-bot: scheduled nightly perf job `ci-kv-trace-probe` created on runner `gpu-ci-8` :calendar: Starting at 03:00 UTC daily.
mia: two implementation notes:
- keep the full qdrep for 7 days, but store a compact summary forever (kernel timeline JSON + small stats) to feed the diff dashboard.
- generate a "trace manifest" with metadata (model, batch_size, seq_len, kv_warm=true/false, commit, runner type) so diffs are apples-to-apples.
sam: for the compact summary we can run `nsys stats` or our python extractor to produce per-kernel aggregated rows (name, total_time_ms, calls, avg_ms). That shrinks artifacts a lot and is enough for the regression dashboard.
alex: agree. Naming convention proposal:
`s3://perf-artifacts/env=ci/job=kv-trace-probe/commit={sha}/ts=1765432123/`
inside: `nsys.qdrep`, `summary.json`, `meta.json` (model,batch,seq,kvcache:true,warm_iters:5), `kernels.csv`
jordan: gating idea: when nightly runs land, compute median token latency and p99. If p99 regresses >10% vs baseline or kernel timeline hash changes for the top-5 kernels by time, open a perf-regression ticket and attach both qdrep and summary.
mia: for storage cost control, compress the summary and kernels.csv with gzip and keep qdrep only for failures (i.e., when a regression is detected we promote qdrep to long-term storage for 90 days). Also add a small sampling cap: run at most 3 traces per commit to avoid overload.
sam: example extractor command we can run in CI after nsys finishes:
```
nsys stats -f cudaKernel -i nsys.qdrep -o nsys-summary
python tools/trace_extractor.py --in nsys-summary.qdrep --out summary.json --top 20
```
(note: `tools/trace_extractor.py` will emit the per-kernel table + timeline buckets we need for diffing)
alex: I'll add a CI job that runs on the dedicated GPU pool, runs the workload with warmup, toggles `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_LOG_KERNELS`, captures `nsys`, runs the extractor, uploads summary + meta, and only uploads qdrep if a gate trips. I'll open a PR tonight. @jordan @mia can you volunteer to review the extractor + dashboard ingestion side?
jordan: I can review the ingestion + gating logic. I'll also add a small service that computes kernel-hash diffs and emits a score.
mia: I'll look at the extractor and add KV-related annotations (kv-cache hit rate, prefix-length histogram) to the meta.json. :sparkles:
infra-bot: note: please ensure the CI runner IAM role has `s3:PutObject` to `perf-artifacts/*` and the job image includes `nsys` binary. I'll file infra ticket if missing.
alex: perfect. Also let's add a quick doc snippet in `eng-runtime/README` describing the job and the manifest fields so future folks can reproduce locally. Planning to land PR by EOD.
sam: LGTM, thanks alex. :thumbsup:
perf-ci-bot: nightly `ci-kv-trace-probe` queued for 03:00 UTC (will post results to /dash/perf-diff).
alex: thanks everyone — I'll post the PR link here when ready.
